belief: I am what I do for a living.
origins: “What do you do?” is often the first question we are asked, and the answer can quietly become who we are. A family that prized a certain career, a profession with long training, or a parent whose identity was their job can teach us to merge the two. This works while the job is going well. When the role changes, ends, or disappoints, the person underneath can feel lost.
teaches: Scripture honors work. God worked in creation, and Paul tells us to work with our whole being, as for the Lord. But Scripture places identity before work. We are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, and the works come from who we are, not the other way around. We are made in God’s image and called by Him. A job is one place where we serve, but it is not the name God calls us by.
self_statements: If I am not my job, I do not know who I am.
When people ask what I do, that is who I am.
If my work is ordinary, so am I.
I only matter when I am working.
errors: Believing that my identity is either my job or nothing.
Seeing only the work part of who I am.
Feeling empty when work changes and concluding that I am empty.
questions: If someone asked who I am without using my job, what would I say?
What roles, relationships, and values make up my identity besides work?
What does God call me, and when did He call me that?
How did my family treat work and identity?
What do I lose if I let work define me?
What qualities would remain if my job changed tomorrow?
truth: My work is a good thing I do, not the whole of who I am. I was made in God’s image and made His workmanship in Christ before I did any job. I can do my work well and hold my title loosely.
hw_truths: I am more than my job.
My work flows from who I am, not the reverse.
I can enjoy my work without being defined by it.
God calls me by name, not by title.
log: Each day, write one thing about yourself that has nothing to do with your work.
actions: Complete ten sentences about who you are that do not mention a job.
Next time you meet someone, share something about your family, faith, or interests before your job.
Ask a friend or family member what they value about you besides your work.
prayer: Father, You made me and called me Yours before I did any work. Free me from being defined by my title. Help me work well and rest in who You say I am. Amen.
hw_questions: Who am I without my job?
What do others value in me besides my work?
What would remain if my role changed?
What do I enjoy that has nothing to do with work?
How can I introduce myself differently?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am God’s workmanship, so my identity is more than my job.”
